squishing.title: Lore: The Squishing
squishing.description:
On 21 December 2012, the goddess of discord Eris will kill the goddess of justice Maat by hurling the Omega Tower at her. That has already happened, in the future. What reached this dimension was the throw's echo, sent twenty years backward and across ninety-two dimensions, landing on 21 December 1992 as dimension three's own sky, ours.

The paradox has been fraying the timeline and the stability of all ninety-two dimensions ever since. From 1992 onward, spacetime began knotting itself into localized time-loop bubbles (see: the Rule of 80), and fragments of other dimensions started collapsing into this one, the Empty Empire of Varlenia foremost among them. The damage compounds: by 2012, when the throw finally lands for real, the distortion is expected to make this dimension outright uninhabitable.

Squishing does not strike every dimension evenly. The higher a dimension's number, the faster it unravels, the Green Fields, dimension 77, are already largely uninhabitable. The Omega Tower, driven into the earth by the very throw that started all this, is the one thing still holding the ninety-two dimensions apart from collapsing into each other; without it, by most accounts, they already would have.

ruleOf80.title: Lore: The Rule of 80
ruleOf80.description:
Since the Squishing began, anything that moves faster than 80 kilometers per hour is pulled into the nearest time-loop bubble, a patch of spacetime, from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers across, where the day resets at its end as if it never happened. Once inside, the rule inverts: the only way out is to move outward past 80 km/h again, and staying under that speed keeps you looping.

Bubbles are nearly invisible from the outside, little more than a shimmer in the air at close range, so they are marked on every road map to keep travelers from wandering in by accident. Their number and their size have both been growing since 1992, and both keep climbing as 2012 approaches.

Looping has its own grim comfort: the only way to die for good inside a bubble is to die while moving above 80 km/h, or be struck by something that is. Everything else just resets. The cost is stagnation, the mind adjusts to the repetition faster than most expect, and a looper keeps their memories of every previous day even as the world resets around them. No signal, electronic, mental, or magical, crosses a bubble's edge, which is why carrier pigeons fitted with USB drives (they can hit 90-100 km/h with a tailwind) remain the fastest reliable post between one loop and the next, and why the Truckers Society exists at all: someone has to carry people, goods, and news between communities that live in different bubbles. Bubba's liminal engine is the one known way to drive straight through a bubble without ever slowing below the threshold.

encompassingRoad.title: Lore: The Encompassing Road
encompassingRoad.description:
Every road in every world of the multiverse is, underneath, the same road. Bubba's liminal engine compresses the stretch ahead of a vehicle, and correctly calibrated, it opens onto the Encompassing Road itself: a mode of travel where an ordinary highway exit can lead somewhere else entirely, another place, another dimension, another time, even the Scraps of Creation.

The road predates every driver on it. Trillions of years ago, so the story goes, the concept of a road was born from the God of Asphalt, who paved the first one, and became the first victim of a hit-and-run, run down by a greater god.

magesGuild.title: Lore: The Mages Guild
magesGuild.description:
Founded in 950 BC by King Solomon, the Mages Guild governed the world's hidden balance for millennia before Margaret Thatcher revealed the existence of magic to the entire planet, live, when she deployed it during the Falklands War. In the early 1900s the Guild was refounded by Sir Aleister Crowley under the patronage of the British royal house as a pseudo-chivalric order, which is why its leadership still carries the styles Sir and Lady.

Beyond rebuilding lost technology with magic on behalf of the world's governments, the Guild's stated purpose is defending reality from extradimensional threats and the horrors the Squishing keeps letting in. Internally it is fractured into as many currents as there are schools of magic, but every major decision runs through the Three Pillars, who stand for the past, the present, and the future. As of 2001, the seats are held by Sir Aleister Crowley (the past), Lady Margaret Thatcher (the present), and 'the Father,' Shoko Asahara (the future).

Holding a Pillar's seat halts its holder's aging for as long as they keep it; a Pillar's term normally runs fifty years. Crowley has never once stepped down, and nobody left in the Guild is in any position to make him, he knows spells even the gods have never heard of.

hypercapitalistCollective.title: Lore: Hypercapitalist Collective
hypercapitalistCollective.description:
The Hypercapitalist Collective is a pyramid scheme the size of a continent, running the trade between dimensions. Its members took the Rule of 80 and made it doctrine: by staying above the threshold long enough, their bodies stopped resetting even once they finally stand still, so while the rest of the world loops and forgets, the Collective remembers everything, indefinitely.

That memory is the whole business model. They sell escapes to people trapped in time loops, and they trade absolutely anything else, memories and emotions included. They also hold a monopoly on the one resource nobody can loop their way around: they control every source of clean water left, while everything outside their reach is cut with LSD.

The Collective is at open war with the Archive Foundation, whose radical-transparency doctrine stands directly in the way of a trade empire built on secrecy and leverage, and stands allied with the Gods.

emTheMemoryWitch.title: Lore: Em, the Memory Witch
emTheMemoryWitch.description:
Em was born in 1984 in Wimbledon, Britannia, wanting to be a witch in an age that had filed magic away among the fairy tales. That changed when Margaret Thatcher, who was secretly a power broker within the Mages Guild, needed a focal point for the Solomon Ritual and chose her.

The ritual's price was 92% of her memories. They did not simply vanish, they were forged into the Spear of Memory, the same weapon Eris later used to kill the Father aspect of YHWH. Em woke up alone on Ritual Island on the first of January, 2001, with no past she could recall and a magical power she is still learning to hold.

She has been on the road ever since, riding a camper she shares with Bubba, heading toward a meeting in Beagle that she can barely remember agreeing to.

camelcaseMagic.title: Lore: CamelCase Magic
camelcaseMagic.description:
Every spell cast since the Squishing must be written and spoken in CamelCase: words run together, a capital letter opening each one. It is not stylistic, and it is not optional. FireBall works. 'Fire ball' does not, and speaking it costs the caster dearly for the attempt.

Multi-word formulas belong to a different tier entirely: transcendentals, incantations powerful enough to reshape reality on command, and the exclusive province of gods. A mortal who breaks a spell into separate words has the universe read it as an attempted transcendental and bill them accordingly, anywhere from the loss of their voice to considerably worse.

Grimoires make the rule visible: a spell written wrong on the page begins infecting the neighboring words with copies of itself, and a book left unburned will go on to consume whatever is left beside it. A caster's active spells are chosen while they sleep, each carrying its own cap on daily uses. Slot two spells into the same slot and they fuse into a single temporary spell for as long as it holds; permanent versions of proven combinations can be bought from vending machines, or earned through ritual.

alagaddaCityOfMasks.title: Lore: Alagadda, City of Masks
alagaddaCityOfMasks.description:
[Archive Foundation dossier, incomplete]

Alagadda does not appear on any map the Guild or the Foundation has managed to fix in place, and every field team sent looking for it has come back with a different account of how they got in, if they came back at all. What survives every retelling, and what every witness insists on repeating first, is the one rule the city enforces without exception: every visitor wears a mask, and it does not come off.

Remove it, for any reason, for any length of time, and the city stops counting you as a person. The condition has a name on file, Unperson, and a description consistent across every witness: invisible, untouchable, unable to leave, drifting through streets that no longer register you exist.

Total Disclosure notwithstanding, this is the entirety of what the Foundation is willing to put its name to. Field teams are advised: mask on, mask secured, mask never removed.

ruleOfHeight.title: Lore: The Rule of Height
ruleOfHeight.description: "The higher you climb, the stranger it gets."

omegaTower.title: Lore: The Omega Tower
omegaTower.description:
From outside it looks like a skyscraper climbing impossibly high past the stratosphere, but the Omega Tower is a divine spear: the one Eris hurled in 1992 to kill the goddess of justice Maat. The spear drove hundreds of kilometers into the crust, and at its lowest point, the tip, lies Maat's own body, sunk and sealed inside it.

The Tower pierces and connects all ninety-two dimensions, letting mortals climb to the celestial throne that seats whichever deity currently reigns over all the gods. At the game's opening that seat belongs to Eris, though who sits it can change with what happens outside the Tower's walls, and if the player leaves the Tower alone too long, one of the game's other major characters may decide to climb it and challenge whoever is sitting there, replacing the final boss outright.

It was meant as an ark: in case of apocalypse, it could have carried the whole of humanity into another dimension. Driven into the Earth as it was, it can no longer be moved, and with the Squishing under way it is now the only thing keeping the ninety-two dimensions from collapsing into each other (party members compare it, often, to the flag that holds a burger together). Sealed shut until 31 December 1999, its door opened on its own the night two billion people died during the Y2K event.

Its interior is chaos, both a spacetime anomaly and neutral ground for every faction on Earth: department stores built beside underground jungles, reactors the size of a small city, corridors lined with camping tents. The Archive Foundation was first to explore and settle it, and keeps the peace between the factions that have since opened offices inside.

eris.title: Lore: Eris
eris.description:
For millennia Eris was judged a third-rate deity, and the resentment curdled into a long campaign to claim the celestial throne for herself. Then, sometime in the 1990s, she fell hopelessly in love with a human: a Nuevo-Texan mechanic named Bubba.

They spent years on the road together in his battered camper, robbing banks along Route 666, the highway connecting the Three Americas, using Eris's gift for bending probability to crack any safe on the spot. The relationship ended in December 1992, when a future version of Eris killed the goddess of justice Maat, retroactively, and the present Eris found herself forced back onto the path to ascension so the paradox would not get worse still, on the theory that putting herself back in position to kill Maat in 2012 might one day let her simply choose not to.

Handed the entire judicial system of every dimension with no training for the job, she runs it her way: chaotic and arbitrary, and worse since Bubba started traveling with the witch-wannabe Em. Eris feels nothing but jealousy toward Em, and bends cosmic law and probability alike to make her life miserable.

After the Father aspect of YHWH died on 31 December 2001 during the Solomon Ritual, Eris sat down on the empty celestial throne, and no other god had the nerve to tell her no. Any sentient being, in any dimension, who commits a crime in view of a witness earns a bounty from her, and if caught is teleported straight into her personal court, where she runs billions of trials at once; for the worst offenders she looses judicial ghosts that travel in a straight line until they catch their target. Defendants can plead guilty, plead innocent, or accuse Eris herself and challenge her for the throne. Killing her there empties the seat, and leaves the Tower open to be claimed for a few days before someone else takes it.

theGods.title: Lore: The Gods
theGods.description:
The gods are at open war with the Mages Guild, who they fear might attempt another Solomon Ritual capable of killing them. A god's existence is tied directly to how many people still believe in it, which is why so few deities from antiquity have survived to the present day.

When a god dies that way, of simple neglect, its body turns to stone and falls into the White Desert, and nobody much minds. Deicide is different: the body stays anchored to physical reality and begins to rot, while its consciousness stays alive inside it. The Egyptian goddess of justice Maat is one recent case, her body pierced by the Omega Tower and buried hundreds of kilometers under the crust. The Father aspect of YHWH, the Abrahamic god, is another: his body still orbits the Earth, caught in the same debris field the Kessler Syndrome set loose. Every impact knocks another piece off the corpse, and it is those pieces, not the debris itself, that fall to the ground; whoever touches one gets a share of his power, enough to grant supernatural abilities even to someone who cannot cast a single spell.

scrapsOfCreation.title: Lore: The Scraps of Creation
scrapsOfCreation.description: Small pocket dimensions the gods once used, eons ago, to test their powers and their creativity. They stayed sealed off from the rest of the multiverse until the Squishing began: after 1992 some of them started falling into the physical world on their own, and others became reachable for the first time thanks to Bubba's liminal engine.

liminalEngine.title: Lore: The Liminal Engine
liminalEngine.description:
Bubba's own invention: switched on, it compresses the road ahead of the vehicle, letting it cross an entire continent in minutes while ignoring both the Rule of 80 and the local time-loop bubbles. The first prototype ran in 1996, and after years of testing and misadventures with the witch-wannabe Em, it reached commercial production in 2001. It is now fitted to nearly every public transport vehicle on Earth, which has made Bubba disgustingly rich.

Properly calibrated, the engine can carry a vehicle underwater, through open air, or into space, but only Bubba knows the configuration that tears through spacetime itself and reaches other dimensions, or the Scraps of Creation.

naguka.title: Lore: The Naguka
naguka.description:
Tens of millions of years ago, a common ancestor of Homo sapiens took up permanent residence underground, in the cave system Magamui had dug out ages before. The Naguka evolved alongside surface humans, remaining human enough to interbreed with them, the hybrid offspring are called orcs.

In May 1970 Soviet engineers drilled too deep with the Kola Superdeep Borehole, and the Naguka climbed back up it to begin their invasion of the surface. In the 1990s, campaigning through Scandinavia, they discovered Norwegian black metal, and much of the tribe took to worshipping the band Junehem as gods, painting their faces with corpse paint before battle. The Holy Vatican Empire is the only hyperpower with formal diplomatic ties to the Naguka, though its missionary efforts are really an attempt to convert them into a standing army.

Every Naguka shares access to the Goblin collective unconscious: hurt one, and their entire species turns against you.

verden.title: Lore: The Verden
verden.description:
They look much like the Naguka, gentler features, skin with a blue tint, but where the Naguka are human at heart, the Verden are true goblins, evolved in a different dimension entirely, with a biology to match: they lay eggs, reproduce by fission, and a severed Verden limb planted in soil grows into a new Verden.

They once lived in the Green Fields, dimension 77, one of the most advanced species in the multiverse, until, for reasons even today's Naguka do not know, they gave up all their technology thousands of years before 2001, launched it into their home star, and settled into a bucolic life devoted to the study of magic. Driven out of the Green Fields by the Squishing, they found a new home on Earth and fell in love with its technology in turn. Most are well integrated into human society and speak fluent MarkovSpeak, unlike their Naguka cousins, who still talk like children.

Having studied the Naguka, the Verden learned to read the Goblin collective unconscious with magic and see their moves before they make them, though the access is read-only: they cannot plant new information in it, like a fabricated threat or a way to manipulate the Naguka directly.

junehem.title: Lore: Junehem
junehem.description:
The Norwegian death metal band is midway through deification, driven by mass worship from the Naguka. Over time they have learned to steer the Goblin collective unconscious through their own music, and now lead the goblin hordes trying to push into Europe out of Scandinavia.

The classic lineup is a small pantheon in its own right. Hieronymus, guitar, is the one member who walked away and is worshipped anyway, in absentia, which the Naguka consider a stronger kind of holiness than showing up would be. Mark Bitterness, bass and later vocals, is worshipped loudest and most literally, with shrines that treat his prison record as a martyrdom rather than a conviction. Dauði, the original vocalist, died young and is worshipped as a psychopomp, the one member of the pantheon the Horde prays to before a raid rather than during one. Jarnhand keeps the beat behind all three and is, by most accounts, the only member who finds the whole thing exhausting.

Every government on Earth has tried to kill Junehem by every means available, but killing a god of metal is no longer possible as long as a single goblin still believes in them, and there are, by any count anyone has managed, several million goblins who do.

hieronymus.title: Lore: Hieronymus
hieronymus.description:
He survived being stabbed by his own bandmate Mark Bitterness, and the brain trauma left him with acquired savant syndrome, making him one of the most powerful psionics on the planet. Unlike Mark Bitterness and the rest of Junehem, who live as gods worshipped by the entire Naguka species, Hieronymus walked away from music entirely, and the Horde has never quite forgiven him for it, if forgiveness is even the word for how a species with a collective unconscious processes an absence.

He did not just quit playing. He retreated from the world by every measure that matters: no address, no known face-to-face contact in years, nothing that so much as brushes against a leyline in a way the Guild's own scryers can track. Nobody knows where he went, and the theories range from a monastery to another dimension entirely to the far likelier and far less romantic possibility that he is simply somewhere quiet, being left alone for what might be the first time in his life.

petrodemons.title: Lore: Petrodemons
petrodemons.description:
Entities made of sentient crude oil, effectively indestructible as long as they stay near a leyline, since the leyline keeps regenerating them. Dinosaurs, so the theory goes, were natural arcane practitioners, able to cast without leylines, and some of that lingering power stayed bound to the oil their bodies became.

The only way to weaken one enough to kill it is to deliberately break the leyline it draws on and then attack it with conventional weapons or divine magic, and even without regeneration a Petrodemon is still a fight that needs an army. Most hyperpowers would rather sign contracts with them than fight: Petrodemons can redirect leylines, and that is worth more than the fight is worth winning.

matteiLegend.title: Lore: The Legend of Enrico Mattei
matteiLegend.description: The story goes that Enrico Mattei, founder of the oil company ENI, found a scroll in a Libyan tomb holding the ritual to summon and bind Petrodemons, ancient elementals bound to oil deposits. He is said to have attempted it to win Italy full energy independence, and something went wrong: his plane went down not long after, in 1962. Whether the Petrodemons are real or not, the story has stuck as the tidiest metaphor going for the greed of the oil industry.

kesslerSyndrome.title: Lore: The Kessler Syndrome
kesslerSyndrome.description:
During the Y2K event, the ENVISAT satellite lost control and collided with another, and the chain reaction of debris it triggered has not stopped since. Within a year of 31 December 1999, the cascade had grown dense enough that leaving the atmosphere by rocket or spacecraft became close to suicide: crossing the debris shell around the Earth is compared to walking through a meat grinder, and launch fatality rates now run above ninety percent.

The European Space Agency, under Margherita Hack, is testing new rockets built almost entirely from sacrificial armor plating, designed to be shredded by the debris field while keeping the crew alive long enough to clear orbit, though these craft cannot leave the solar system; their whole purpose is docking with one of the few ships still stationed beyond the debris cloud. Given how dangerous the attempt is, spaceports like the GreenWitch Space Center and the Apulian spaceport at Taranto still take volunteers, free of charge.

The field has one grim silver lining. The petrified corpse of the Father aspect of YHWH still hangs in orbit, and every strike it takes from the debris cloud knocks another fragment loose, sending pieces of a dead god raining down to the surface.

canadafrica.title: Lore: Canadafrica
canadafrica.description: One of the first visible effects of the Squishing: over the course of a single day, the whole of Mexico and South America reshaped itself to match the outline of Africa as seen from space, cities, borders, and all their people left exactly where they were.

serpentineRoad.title: Lore: The Serpentine Road
serpentineRoad.description: A spiraling tunnel opening somewhere in Antarctica, connecting the surface to the Earth's core and to the Inverted Citadel. Magamui dug it hundreds of millions of years ago, on its way down to the core after arriving on Earth.

magamui.title: Lore: Magamui
magamui.description:
An alien larva a quarter the size of the Moon, wrapped around the Earth's core for millions of years, feeding on the heat and electromagnetism the core produces. Dormant as it is, it can still seize mental control of one person at a time, mostly to keep itself safe, and there is reason to think that ability could extend to the entire human population if it ever reaches full maturity. Should it ever leave the Earth to return to space, the effects would be catastrophic.

Part of the Mages Guild's job is finding whoever is currently under Magamui's control and killing them, since taking hold of a new host costs Magamui time it would rather not spend.

invertedCitadel.title: Lore: The Inverted Citadel
invertedCitadel.description:
Built inside a vast cavern Magamui carved around the Earth's core, with the core itself hanging at the center like a sun. The city wraps entirely around it, shell-like, so that looking straight up shows other districts of the same city on the far side of the core.

It was raised by an advanced civilization that lived on Earth somewhere between the age of the dinosaurs and the rise of humanity, and vanished without leaving behind a single written record or a scrap of surviving technology, just an empty city. Over time it became the underground capital of the Goblins.

vaticanEmpire.title: Lore: The Holy Vatican Empire
vaticanEmpire.description:
A Catholic theocracy ruling Italy, Spain, Poland, and East Germany, the direct successor to the Holy Roman Empire. Power is split between throne and altar: the Pope holds the whole empire together while local government is left to the politicians of each member state. Only sacred magic and technomancy are permitted within its borders, with very few exceptions; arcane practitioners caught casting are burned at the stake, or, more rarely, recruited into the Umbra Excidii, the arcane order tasked with hunting down other arcane casters on Vatican soil.

The current Pope took the name Peter II; born Joseph Ratzinger, he was elected after the death of John Paul II, killed in the assassination attempt of 13 May 1981. Vatican City carries a battery of liminal engines, and after the death of the Father aspect of YHWH it was fully militarized into the Vatican Citadel, hovering roughly 800 meters above Rome, with a battery of Gauss cannons ready for any unbeliever who gets too close. Peter II has declared Jenna of Northpoint the Antichrist and gone to war with her rather than recognize her as the Second Coming.

okeanus.title: Lore: Okeanus
okeanus.description:
The ultimate water spell, the one that traumatized the whole planet live on television during the Falklands War. It lets the caster control an entire mass of water at once, and was used to annihilate the Argentine fleet, swallowing ships whole and cutting sailors and soldiers in half with pressurized jets of water.

Its use, military and public alike, revealed to the world that magic was real, and set off an arms race in battle magic among every hyperpower on Earth.

theonuclearBombingNewYork.title: Lore: The Theonuclear Bombing of New York
theonuclearBombingNewYork.description:
On 11 September 2001, members of a Thatcherist cell detonated three theonuclear devices in the heart of New York. The blasts did almost no structural damage, but disintegrated every soul within their radius, leaving empty shells behind, bodies still moving on instinct and biology alone with nothing left inside.

The attack was blamed on Al-Qaeda. Only the Three Pillars of the Mages Guild know the truth: the bombs were built from artifacts consumed by the Solomon Ritual, their spent potential converted into a weapon instead of simply discarded.

solomonRitual.title: Lore: The Solomon Ritual
solomonRitual.description:
An elaborate rite spanning a full night, requiring the Mages Guild's Three Pillars, one sacrifice, and seven artifacts of genuine historical or esoteric weight. Every artifact used loses all of its power in the process, though the potential it never got to spend can be converted into a theonuclear device.

It was last performed on 31 December 2001, exactly one year after the Y2K event, with the Iron Crown once worn by Holy Roman Emperors and later by the Popes of the Vatican Empire, the Spear of Longinus, the mythic sword Tyrfing out of Norse legend, clay from the Golem of Prague, the draconic clasp of Xia out of 2070 BC China, and a bone carved into a horn, of Neolithic origin.

The ritual rewrites magic's own source code within whatever dimension it is cast in, and can make spellcasting trivial for anyone, restrict it to a chosen few, or shut it off entirely. Magic is thought to have stayed a fairy tale through the Renaissance and into the modern era precisely because so few people had access to it; Aleister Crowley rediscovered the ritual and used it early in the 1900s to open magic up to the world at large, quietly. The 2001 casting had a different purpose: draining every memory and every scrap of future potential out of the witch-wannabe Em, who volunteered as the sacrifice, and forging them into a spear able to kill the Father aspect of YHWH, the Abrahamic god, whose soul was shattered into quadrillions of fragments and whose rotting body still orbits the Earth. Em survived it, but lost ninety-two percent of her memories, and for reasons nobody has explained, came out of it with far more magical potential than she went in with.

Smaller versions of the ritual exist, reshaping how magic behaves locally with a single artifact instead of seven, but the effects do not last, and the caster risks death or memory loss every time.

fantablack.title: Lore: Fantablack
fantablack.description:
A pigment scraped from the outer skin of the Omega Tower: anything painted with it becomes immune to localized time-loop bubbles, and the inside of every vehicle fitted with a liminal engine is lined with it. It runs expensive, but bullets and blades coated in Fantablack can kill a person even inside a time loop.

The same pigment is milled into euro banknotes, and its arcane properties, combined with the rule that names carry power, are what let Mario Draghi ascend to godhood in the first place.

anokiPhones.title: Lore: Anoki Phones
anokiPhones.description: The first working example of technology rebuilt through magic: these bricks draw on leylines to reach each other, and properly tuned, can be used to call the afterlife, or the gods themselves directly. No trucker leaves home without one in their pocket.

arcaneMagic.title: Lore: Arcane Magic
arcaneMagic.description:
Magic bends reality to intent, and nobody has ever managed to explain it cleanly, the harder anyone studies it, the less rational it gets, though a handful of rules have held steady for decades, the law of CamelCase chief among them.

It runs along leylines, invisible rivers of power that rise out of oil deposits and connect places of historical, religious, or arcane weight. The closer a caster stands to one, the more raw power a spell carries, and the harder that power is to control; casting directly on top of a leyline without proper training can snap it outright, and a broken leyline makes even the simplest spell a fight, with the exception of divine magic, which runs on rules different enough to sit in a category of its own. Spells cast far from any leyline still work, just weaker, which is why so much of a mage's actual job is geography: finding the spot that does the most damage.

There are three ways to cast. Ritual magic is open to anyone who is not a complete idiot: follow the steps without a single mistake and the spell goes off with no MP cost at all, the most powerful kind there is, and nearly impossible to undo short of a counter-ritual. Sympathetic magic compresses an entire ritual into words, hand gestures, and catalyst materials, trading hours of preparation for seconds, at the cost of MP; weaker than ritual magic, but fast. Metamagic replaces every physical component of a sympathetic spell, words, gestures, catalysts, with pure imagination, and its effects can be multiplied together to build entirely new spells; generally the weakest of the three, but silent, castable by thought alone. It is often mistaken for psionics, which is not magic at all and runs on entirely different rules.

sacredMagic.title: Lore: Sacred Magic
sacredMagic.description:
Where arcane magic rises out of oil deposits and runs along leylines, sacred magic comes down from the gods themselves, granted to whoever worships and calls on them. It shares arcane magic's three casting methods, ritual, sympathetic, and meta, but can also take the form of outright miracles with no scientific or magical explanation at all, violating every rule everything else has to follow.

Sacred magic stops working the moment its god dies. Most of the sacred spells the Vatican once relied on have been all but useless since 31 December 2001, when the Father aspect of YHWH died.

truckersSociety.title: Lore: The Truckers Society
truckersSociety.description: The real knights of the Road. They do not just haul cargo, they keep the connections alive between communities living in different, mutually inaccessible realities, running their own internal hierarchy and a dense network for trading word of what waits further down the highway. None of them leave home without an old Anoki phone in their pocket.

marioDraghi.title: Lore: Mario Draghi
marioDraghi.description:
Mario Draghi's name is printed on tens of billions of banknotes and logged across more financial transactions than God's name appears in every printed Bible on Earth combined. The security strip woven into every euro note is milled from scraps of Fantablack scraped off the Omega Tower's outer skin, and between that ritual component and the rule that names carry power, Draghi ascended to become the god of markets, losing his individual identity and physical body in the exchange and becoming an abstract concept instead: the financial engine quietly running the multiverse's economy from behind the scenes.

Unlike other gods, whose survival depends on how many people believe in them, killing Mario Draghi would take burning every banknote that carries his name.

ladyThatcher.title: Lore: Lady Margaret Thatcher
ladyThatcher.description:
Long before Margaret Thatcher stood in front of the cameras during the Falklands War and drowned the Argentine fleet with Okeanus, she was already deep inside the Mages Guild, one of its more discreetly powerful members long before the world had any idea magic was real. By the time the Guild's Three Pillars needed a new face for the present, hers was the obvious choice.

Years before the Solomon Ritual, she took in a girl who wanted, more than anything, to be a witch, and taught her real magic herself. It was never kindness. Thatcher was shaping Em into a vessel with exactly the right shape and exactly the right potential to be drained clean during the ritual, the perfect sacrifice, chosen and built for the part years in advance.

What she had not planned for was the aftermath. Stripped of ninety-two percent of her memories, Em came out of the ritual with far more raw potential than she went in with, and somewhere in the wreckage taught herself metamagic without a single lesson, something the Guild's own record books call next to unheard of. Thatcher watches her former student's growth now with something closer to unease than pride: a metamagician who arrived there on her own answers to no doctrine the Guild ever gave her.

aleisterCrowley.title: Lore: Sir Aleister Crowley
aleisterCrowley.description:
Refounded early in the 1900s under the patronage of the British royal house, Sir Aleister Crowley rebuilt the Mages Guild as a pseudo-chivalric order, which is why its leadership still carries the styles Sir and Lady. He has held the Guild's Past seat, one of the Three Pillars, ever since, and has never once agreed to step down; nobody left in the Guild is in any position to make him, since he knows spells even the gods have never heard of.

Before any of that, in April 1900, he tried to seize the Vault of the Adepti from the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, marching on 36 Blythe Road dressed as a Highlander with a black mask and a golden Celtic cross on his chest. W.B. Yeats and a handful of other members physically threw him down the stairs. What the Golden Dawn's own minutes call 'the Battle of Blythe Road' ends there, in every account anyone is allowed to read. What actually happened after Crowley picked himself up off the pavement does not appear in any surviving record: the page is there, the date is there, and everything in between has been [REDACTED] since the night it was written. Whatever he called up onto Blythe Road that evening, it is the one working of his career the Guild has never let anyone catalogue.

Holding a Pillar's seat halts its holder's aging for as long as they keep it, but the body underneath still ages by other means, and wears out by them too. Crowley's current vessel is failing, and everyone in the Guild knows he needs a new one to keep on being immortal. What he intends to become, and what he intends to become it in, is a question the rest of the Three Pillars would very much like answered before he goes ahead and does it.

In 1918 he summoned Lam, a member of the species he calls the Tourists and everyone else calls the Greys. The working only ran one way: Lam came through, and nothing Crowley tried afterward could send it back, so Lam has been stuck on Earth ever since. Crowley has never once said what he asked it, or what it told him. He also despises the Guild's Future Pillar, 'the Father' Shoko Asahara, openly and without apology, though no one has yet been willing to find out whether that contempt would survive an actual challenge for the seat.

shokoAsahara.title: Lore: The Father, Shoko Asahara
shokoAsahara.description:
Before he was one of the Mages Guild's Three Pillars, Shoko Asahara led a cult responsible for one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in living memory, a mass poisoning that killed and maimed by the thousands. Within the Guild he is known, more quietly, as a master of levitation, a genuine practitioner whose power was never in doubt even when his methods were.

His seat among the Three Pillars, representing the future, is the Guild's most disputed appointment: nobody outside the inner circle has ever gotten a straight answer for why a convicted mass murderer was handed a say over what magic becomes next. Sir Aleister Crowley, who holds the Past seat, despises him openly and has never bothered to hide it, though whether that contempt runs any deeper than words has never actually been tested.

blytheRoadBattle.title: Lore: The Battle of Blythe Road
blytheRoadBattle.description:
On the evening of 17 April 1900, the poet W. B. Yeats stood on the stairs at 36 Blythe Road, London, and refused to let a young occultist calling himself Count Vladimir Svareff past him. The man on the stairs was Aleister Crowley, dressed in Highland tartan, a black mask, and a golden Celtic cross, come to seize the Vault of the Adepti and the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn's inner leadership by force after a schism over who had the right to run it. Yeats, already a senior member of the Order and no stranger to ritual himself, did not argue with him. He and two other Adepti simply picked Crowley up and threw him down the stairs.

The Order's own minutes record the rest as a formality: police called, no charges filed, Crowley barred from the premises. Yeats wrote almost nothing about that night afterward, in poetry or in private letters, which those who knew him took as its own kind of statement. Guild historians read the silence differently. Every surviving account of the Battle of Blythe Road ends at the bottom of the stairs, at the exact moment Crowley got back up, and whatever the Order's minutes originally said about what happened next has been [REDACTED] ever since, in a hand nobody in the Guild will admit to recognizing.

theTourists.title: Lore: The Tourists
theTourists.description:
The Tourists is what the Zeta Reticulans call themselves, and Greys is what everyone else calls them. Their homeworld sits thirty-nine light years out, which is exactly how long it took Earth's first radio and television broadcasts to reach it: they only found out humanity existed in 1975, and did not get quietly involved in world affairs before that date. Officially, first contact came in 1999. Unofficially, a handful of earlier encounters had already leaked into human folklore long before either side admitted to anything.

They are, by every account anyone has managed to get out of one, obsessed with humanity, and especially with its television. Somewhere off Earth they have built an enormous monument to the species, and Guild diplomats who have seen it describe it less as a statue than as a standing ovation cast in something that is not quite metal. They mean no one on this planet any harm, and in every recorded instance they have gone out of their way to avoid hurting a human being or a human government even when it would have been easier not to bother.

What they are genuinely good at is a short list, and everything on it involves bending spacetime: they mastered faster-than-light travel and gravity manipulation long before they had any concept of Earth, and have since built two working Dyson spheres around their home star. Any human ship that makes it out to Zeta Reticuli gets a free refuel from them, no questions asked, one more expression of the same fondness that built the monument.

They tried to start a third one around the Sun, meant as a gift more than anything Earth actually needed. The first mirror they put in place lasted about as long as it took a stray fragment of the Kessler debris to find it, and they have not tried again since, though the wreckage is still up there, drifting, one more thing for the debris field to eventually reclaim.

Outside of gravity and light-speed, they are close to hopeless, and lean on human science and human magic for almost everything else they need done, which makes their attempts to help clear the Kessler debris field a little painful to watch. They mean well: since the field sealed off low orbit they have been trying, more or less continuously, to clean it out. They are just bad at it, and a disappointing number of cleanup runs end with a Tourist vessel clipped by the very debris it came to collect.

theDargos.title: Lore: The Dargos
theDargos.description:
Where the Tourists are recent arrivals, the Dargos have known about Earth since before there were words for what they were doing to it. Nobody in the Guild has ever managed to have a real conversation with one; what contact exists comes entirely through abduction, and through pranks specific enough, and cruel enough, that 'trolling' has become the polite term for it in official reports.

They do not seem to want anything from humanity beyond the reaction. A Dargos encounter rarely leaves lasting physical harm and just as rarely leaves the victim believed by anyone who was not there, which several Guild researchers suspect is closer to the actual point than any of the usual theories about genetic sampling or invasion scouting.

hillIncident.title: Lore: The Hill Incident
hillIncident.description:
On the night of 19 September 1961, Betty and Barney Hill were driving home through the White Mountains when a craft forced their car to stop, and both of them lost close to two hours they have never been able to fully account for. Their story became the first widely publicized abduction case in the country, and Betty's sketch of a star map she claimed to have seen aboard the craft has been argued over for decades since.

In one detail every published account of the story gets wrong, because none of them could have known it: the craft that took the Hills never made it home. Trying to return to Zeta Reticuli, it was shot down by the wards Aleister Crowley had already laid across Earth's approaches, and never reported back what it found. The Tourists would not learn Earth existed for another fourteen years, and when they finally did, it was over the radio, not from anything the Hills' abductors had time to send.

zanfrettaIncident.title: Lore: The Zanfretta Incident
zanfrettaIncident.description:
Pier Fortunato Zanfretta was working a quiet night shift as a security guard outside Genoa on 6 December 1978 when the first encounter happened, and it did not stop there: over the following years he reported being visited again and again, by beings that got taller, stranger, and harder to believe with every retelling.

Guild researchers who eventually looked into it stopped treating it as a single event and started treating it as a running bit. The consensus, such as it is, points to the Dargos: nothing about the case fits a genuine research or contact effort, but all of it fits a species that had found someone gullible and telegenic and simply kept coming back to see what he would say next.

jennaOfNorthpoint.title: Lore: Jenna of Northpoint
jennaOfNorthpoint.description:
Jenna of Northpoint claims to be the Second Coming, the reincarnation of Jesus Christ, and enough people believe her that the claim carries real weight in a world where belief is what keeps a god alive. She did not arrive preaching. She arrived running a business, and the first thing she did with it was gut Northpoint's arena from the inside.

The arena had spent decades running death matches before she took it over. She kept the crowds, kept the wagering, kept every bit of the spectacle, and cut out the killing: choreography and real athletic skill standing in for what used to be a body count. Sir Peter II has never accepted her claim, and declared her the Antichrist instead of a returned messiah, going so far as to take the Holy Vatican Empire to war over the refusal alone. Jenna has not answered in kind. She keeps running her bloodless arena, and keeps letting his war make her case for her.

popePetrusII.title: Lore: Pope Petrus II
popePetrusII.description:
Born Joseph Ratzinger, he took the name Petrus II after John Paul II was killed in the assassination attempt of 13 May 1981, an attack Guild intervention could not reach in time. Where his predecessor is remembered as protected by destiny, Petrus II is remembered as the pope who militarized it.

After the Father aspect of YHWH died in 2001, he had Vatican City rebuilt into the Vatican Citadel, a fortress that now hovers roughly 800 meters over Rome behind a battery of Gauss cannons, ready for any unbeliever who gets too close. He has declared Jenna of Northpoint the Antichrist and taken the Holy Vatican Empire to war against her rather than accept her claim to be the Second Coming, a war fought so far mostly in press releases and border skirmishes, since Jenna has shown no interest in fighting back.

maat.title: Lore: Maat
maat.description:
Maat was the Egyptian goddess of justice, order, and truth long before any of the current pantheon's politics existed, weighing the hearts of the dead against a single feather and finding most of them wanting. She survived millennia of shrinking worship better than most of her contemporaries, right up until Eris, in a version of 2012 that has technically not happened yet, killed her by throwing the Omega Tower at her.

That murder is the whole of the Squishing's original sin. Maat's body is down at the Tower's tip, driven hundreds of kilometers under the crust and sealed there since 1992, her consciousness still intact inside a corpse that cannot move and cannot die twice. Nobody has found a way to free her, or a ritual that would not risk making the paradox worse than it already is.

falklandsWar.title: Lore: The Falklands War
falklandsWar.description:
The war itself was a minor colonial dispute over a scatter of islands nobody outside Argentina and Britannia much cared about, right up until Margaret Thatcher stepped in front of the cameras and cast Okeanus. Live, in front of the entire watching planet, she drowned the Argentine fleet in a wall of pressurized water, cutting ships and sailors alike in half.

That broadcast is the day the world found out magic was real. Governments that had spent decades pretending otherwise scrambled to catch up, and the arms race that followed, every hyperpower on Earth racing to build its own battle magic, traces back to those few minutes of footage more directly than to anything the war was actually fought over.

varlenia.title: Lore: The Empty Empire of Varlenia
varlenia.description:
The Empty Empire of Varlenia was, by every account anyone has been able to piece together, a nation in some other dimension entirely, one of the first casualties of the Squishing's habit of letting fragments of other realities collapse into this one. What is left of it on Earth now is not a place so much as an absence: streets, buildings, and city grids that behave like Varlenia's without a single Varlenian left to explain why.

Guild survey teams treat a Varlenia fragment as one of the more dangerous things the Squishing has produced, not because anything in it attacks, but because nothing in it does anything at all, and the silence has a way of getting into people who stay too long.

threeAmericas.title: Lore: The Three Americas
threeAmericas.description:
Independence never fully happened here, and the continent split three ways instead of one. On the east coast sits the Republic of Cascadia. The center belongs to the Free States of Midwest, an unbroken line of Lincolns on the currency with Bill Clinton presently holding the chair. The west coast never broke from Britannia at all: it is the Atlantic Protectorate, administered by a dynasty of colonial Cornwallises now nine generations deep into a war that, here, never really ended. Nobody has bothered fixing the compass directions on any of the three names since the Squishing started scrambling the maps.

The three barely acknowledge each other exists. What passes for a shared identity travels the roads between them instead of through any of their capitals, carried by the same truckers who carry everything else.

goblinHorde.title: Lore: The Goblin Horde
goblinHorde.description:
The Horde is what the Naguka became once they had a government to speak of, and its leadership reads less like a cabinet than like a monster manual: the Great Goblin at the top, and under him a rotating cast of chieftains named Griznak, Krazz, Zog, Skab, Blight, and a dozen others who answer to nobody but him and not for long. It runs out of Iceland now, the closest solid ground to the Kola Superdeep Borehole the Horde first climbed out of in May 1970.

The Horde does not do diplomacy so much as it does raids that occasionally stop, and the only hyperpower with anything like a working relationship to it is the Holy Vatican Empire, whose missionaries keep trying to convert a species that mostly just wants to be left alone with its Junehem records.

kukulkanAscendancy.title: Lore: The Kukulkan Ascendancy
kukulkanAscendancy.description:
Mexico's hyperpower answers, on paper, to a lineage that starts with a literal god-emperor: Kukulkan first, then a procession of divine Ajaws, jaguar generals, and calendar keepers stretching back further than anyone still alive can verify. Then, without much fuss made of the transition, the leadership rolls straight into Porfirio Diaz, Madero, Zapata, Villa, and every other name out of the real Mexican Revolution, as if the twentieth century had simply been the latest chapter of the same unbroken succession.

Nobody in the Ascendancy treats this as strange. Whether Kukulkan actually still sits somewhere behind the modern presidency, or whether the throne is just a very old habit the country never got around to breaking, is not a question its own citizens spend much time asking.

dprkorea.title: Lore: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea
dprkorea.description: The Kim line runs the Democratic People's Republic of Korea the way it always has, father to son to grandson, with a small permanent bench of party men filling out whatever the family does not want to bother with directly. What sets this timeline's version apart is not the politics, which nobody outside the country gets to see clearly enough to judge, but how thoroughly the personality cult has become load-bearing: state media does not just praise the Kims, it insists on impossible things about them, weather control and instant mastery and effortless victory, with the kind of consistency that starts to look less like propaganda and more like an actual claim.

dharmaDirectorate.title: Lore: The Dharma Directorate
dharmaDirectorate.description:
China's government wears two faces stitched together and does not see the seam. One is the familiar one: Sun Yat-sen, Chiang Kai-shek, Mao, and the long unbroken line of General Secretaries after him, running the largest bureaucracy on the continent exactly as history remembers it. The other sits half a step behind the first, in titles the outside world rarely hears: a Grand Preceptor, an Abbot Chancellor, a Harmony Regent, an entire shadow clergy of the Directorate's own invention, blessing decisions the Politburo has already made.

Which face actually runs the country on a given day depends entirely on who you ask, and the Directorate has never seen a reason to settle the question for outsiders.

illuminatedKhanate.title: Lore: The Illuminated Khanate
illuminatedKhanate.description: Mongolia rules itself as a fusion nobody planned for on purpose: half khanate, half Buddhist theocracy, with an Illuminated Khan on one side of the throne and a line of Bogd Khans and lama regents on the other, each supplying legitimacy the other cannot manufacture alone. It is a small hyperpower by every material measure, population and economy both, and stays a hyperpower anyway on the strength of a monastic tradition of magic that treats spellcraft as a form of prayer, and prayer as a discipline nobody outside the Khanate has bothered to master half as well.

solomonicRepublic.title: Lore: The Solomonic Republic
solomonicRepublic.description:
Israel's government is, quite literally, the court of King Solomon, still in session three thousand years later. The Republic's ministers are not politicians in any sense the rest of the world would recognize: Nasi Prince Sitri, Temple Scribe Duke Bathin, Keeper of the Seal Earl Bifrons, entities out of the same Goetic tradition Solomon is famous for binding into service, still bound, still legislating.

The Ritual that carries Solomon's name gets the credit, or the blame, and the Republic is the clearest surviving proof that the original working was never just theory: seventy-two spirits given office instead of exorcism, running a functioning state on the strength of a three-thousand-year-old contract none of them have ever been able to break.

petroKingdomOfArabia.title: Lore: The Petro Kingdom of Arabia
petroKingdomOfArabia.description: Arabia's monarchy runs on the same resource its titles are named after: an Oil Emir, a Well Sheikh, a Concession Regent, before the line settles into the familiar House of Saud and its kings. What the titles do not advertise is how literally some of that oil talks back. Petrodemons cluster thickest under Arabian sand, and the Kingdom's entire foreign policy runs, more than it admits out loud, on contracts renewed with things that were old before Islam and will very likely outlast the monarchy that currently signs the paperwork.

sanatanaRashtra.title: Lore: Sanatana Rashtra
sanatanaRashtra.description: India governs itself as a Dharma Directorate of its own kind, though nobody there calls it that: a Dharma Regent and an Acharya sit alongside, not above, a parliamentary line running through Nehru, Indira Gandhi, and Vajpayee, each accepted as the political expression of the same order the Regent represents in ritual. The Rashtra is the one hyperpower on the continent that never bothered separating its magic from its government in the first place, on the theory that a state without dharma is not a state worth keeping.

longChile.title: Lore: Long Chile
longChile.description: Chile calls itself the Long South, and mostly means it geographically: a nation of a single impossibly narrow strip mapped out first by a Marshal of the Long South and a Cordillera General before the twentieth century's real presidents, Ibanez, Alessandri, Pinochet among them, take over the record. The military titles never really went away even after the civilian ones showed up; they just moved into an honorary tier the hyperpower keeps dusted off for ceremony, and for the moments when the ceremony stops being enough.

imperialStatePersia.title: Lore: The Imperial State of Persia
imperialStatePersia.description: Persia's monarchy simply never had the revolution history remembers: the Qajar shahs hand off cleanly to the Pahlavis, Reza Shah to Mohammad Reza to Reza Pahlavi II, with Mossadegh's premiership folded into the record as an interruption rather than a rupture. Shahbanu Farah appears in the succession as more than a consort, a working head of state in her own right whenever the throne needed one. The Imperial State treats its own continuity as its main export: proof, to anyone who asks, that a monarchy only falls when it agrees to.
